The fresh single-VM chain reported first-apply changed=1, second-apply changed=0,
and verify PASS (pass=1, fail=0, skip=0). Its synthetic
inline API-token source was discovered, absent from the published record,
and the output scan had no hits.

`evidence_fail_after_mutation=true` failed L4 after changing the managed file.
`evidence_non_idempotent=true` made the real L6 apply return an Ansible success
code while reporting changed tasks. Both backends recorded the intended failed
step and successful rollback; none of the four faults advanced `LATEST.md`.

All six effective-state probes exited 0. Single-VM probes confirmed the original
`pr225-evidence-v1` content in `/etc/pilot-pr225-evidence.conf`; on each topology
node they confirmed the newly created file was absent after rollback.
Fault arms were isolated by reprovisioning between rollback runs. The ephemeral
chain removed both nodes, and final teardown removed all PR225 targets.
Existing user VMs were preserved.

Raw output, generated per-arm records and the fingerprinted matrix driver are

## Not covered / limits (fill in)

This bounded Ubuntu 24.04 KVM test uses a real managed file, Ansible, verification
and libvirt snapshots. It does not validate production role behavior, service
upgrades, other distributions or cross-version migrations. The binary was built
from an isolated Git archive with VCS stamping disabled; full commit/tree were
supplied explicitly and execution-input hashes remained frozen.

Resolver v5 conservatively marks repository `ansible.cfg`, the fixture's
command task and expressions (including conservatively included group-vars
examples) as unresolved. Automatic reuse supports a bounded task subset;
only proven literal copy and debug.msg layouts can qualify. Unsupported actions,
templates, custom modules/plugins and argument layouts fail closed.
These records support the exact tested candidate and evidence-only descendants;
they do not establish automatic evidence reuse after importing a new base.

A prior candidate's subsequent Ansible operation stalled after rollback,
consistent with a stale host-side SSH ControlMaster session. The final matrix
reprovisioned between fault arms and checked effective recovery before teardown.
Repeated Ansible use of an existing restored SSH session is outside this evidence;
this is not a connection-lifecycle fix.

VM chains used synthetic secrets only. Separate real-subprocess regressions cover
stderr-only and JSON-escaped disclosures, ancestor/scalar secrets and stdout
semantics amid stderr. Unknown, encrypted or arbitrarily encoded secrets are
outside the statically discovered-source scan.
